items.title: Alan Raph interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001
items.q: Lew Van Haney was the second trombone player with the New York Philharmonic. And Benny and two other guys from the Basie band studied with Lew.

ctx.x: I didn’t know Benny Powell played bass trombone.

Benny studied with me. Lew Van Haney was the second trombone player with the New York Philharmonic. And Benny and two other guys from the Basie band studied with Lew. And Van Haney moved out to Indiana to take a job teaching there. And I inherited Benny Powell as a student. Benny studied with me for a couple of years. We got to be really good friends. We don’t see each other a lot now, but we are good friends. We know each other and we enjoy each other. And Benny in those days was studying bass trombone with me,…
Yeah. A real gentleman. © Fillius Jazz Archive -10-
